zero_omission_notes.summary: Following the collapse of the Gupta Empire, political power fragmented into regional dynasties across North, Central, and South India. This chapter details Harshavardhana of Kannauj, Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas, the Pallavas of Kanchipuram, the Rashtrakutas, Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and early Cholas. Key themes include the Tripartite Struggle, land grant economies (Brahmadeya), local village assemblies (Sabha, Ur), and rock-cut/structural temple architecture.

detailed_sections.full_notes: King Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) unified northern territories from Kannauj, chronicled by court poet Banabhatta and Chinese scholar Xuanzang. In the Deccan, Chalukya King Pulakeshin II halted Harsha's southward expansion at the Narmada River.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Xuanzang at Nalanda
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Xuanzang spent several years studying at Nalanda Mahavihara, describing its multi-storeyed brick libraries, entrance examinations, and thousands of scholars.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Between the 8th and 10th centuries, the Palas (Bengal), Gurjara-Pratiharas (Malwa), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan) fought over imperial Kannauj. Kings granted tax-free land (Brahmadeya) to Brahmins recorded on copper plates. Subordinate chieftains (Samantas) supplied military contingents. In South India, local self-governance functioned through the Sabha (Brahmin assembly) and Ur (general assembly).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Copper Plate Inscriptions
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Examine royal seals and Sanskrit/Tamil land grant records detailing village boundaries and tax exemptions.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Temple art reached monumental heights: Pallava Shore Temple at Mamallapuram, Rashtrakuta Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora (carved top-down from a single rock), and Chalukya temples at Pattadakal. The Bhakti movement gained momentum through Nayanar (Shaivite) and Alvar (Vaishnavite) saint-poets.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ellora Monolith
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: The Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora (Cave 16) was excavated from a basalt cliff top-down under Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: To analyze the Kudavolai secret ballot voting system recorded in the Uttaramerur Inscriptions.
materials_or_prerequisites: Simulated palm-leaf tickets and earthenware pot
procedure_or_steps: Write eligible candidates' names on palm-leaf tickets based on property, age (35-70), and educational qualifications.
Place tickets inside a sealed clay pot.
A young child draws tickets out one by one in front of the assembly to select committee members (variyars).
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Demonstrates early medieval grassroots democratic procedures with strict eligibility and disqualification criteria (e.g., failing to submit accounts).
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Local rural assemblies in South India exercised structured self-governance independent of central royal court interference.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Tax-free land or entire village gifted by kings to Brahmins to encourage learning and agricultural expansion.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Recorded on copper-plate charters with royal seals.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A subordinate chieftain or vassal ruler who provided military troops and tribute to an overlord king.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Feudal lords under Rashtrakutas or Gurjara-Pratiharas.

textbook_exercises.question: What was the Tripartite Struggle and which dynasties participated in it?
textbook_exercises.answer: The Tripartite Struggle was a centuries-long conflict among the Palas (Bengal), Gurjara-Pratiharas (North/West), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan) for control over imperial Kannauj and the fertile Gangetic plain.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Who was the author of Harshacharita?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Banabhatta was the court poet of King Harshavardhana.

short_answer_questions.question: Differentiate between the Sabha and the Ur in South Indian village administration.
short_answer_questions.answer: Sabha was the autonomous assembly of Brahmin landholders in Brahmadeya villages. Ur was the general assembly of landholders in non-Brahmadeya villages.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: How did royal land grants (Brahmadeya) help expand agriculture during the 6th-10th centuries?
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Land grants encouraged Brahmin scholars to settle uncultivated or forest lands, introduce advanced iron ploughing and irrigation techniques, bring fresh land under cultivation, and integrate local tribes into agrarian society.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Describe the administrative, artistic, and educational achievements under the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer:
Administrative: Maintained strong armies, utilized Samantas, and supported rural village autonomy.
Artistic: Chalukyas built rock-cut caves at Badami and structural temples at Pattadakal (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Rashtrakutas excavated the breathtaking monolithic Kailashanatha Temple at Ellora.
Educational: Royal patronage supported universities, Sanskrit learning, Jain philosophy, and literature (e.g., Amoghavarsha's Kavirajamarga).

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: An archaeologist unearths a 9th-century copper plate in Tamil Nadu specifying rules for electing village committee members by drawing palm-leaf tickets from an earthen pot.

qa.question: What historical voting system is recorded on this copper plate?
qa.answer: The Kudavolai system of secret ballot election.

qa.question: What disqualification rule was enforced under this system?
qa.answer: Candidates who failed to submit financial accounts for their previous tenure were disqualified from contesting.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Believing post-Gupta India was in a state of complete civilisational decline.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: It was an era of intense regional state formation, flourishing temple architecture, oceanic trade expansion, and educational vibrancy.
